claims.text: A predictive model integrating detailed local-disorder descriptors can identify low-lattice-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional ab initio or empirical approaches.
Mass fluctuations, atomic-size mismatch, and force-constant fluctuations are relevant descriptors of phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
The intended initial materials are single-phase, chemically homogeneous high-entropy alloys.
FeCoCrMnNi is a five-element random alloy.
Force-constant fluctuations of about 20% contribute to acoustic-phonon attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi.
FeCoCrMnNi has moderate lattice thermal conductivity.
A machine-learning model trained on binary-alloy data and equipped with a transformation module can be used to screen and rank high-entropy-alloy compositions.
Thermal transport and inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering measurements should be performed at room temperature or application-relevant elevated temperatures.
Using an inert atmosphere will minimize extrinsic effects in the proposed measurements.
Mass variance, atomic-radius mismatch, and force-constant or chemical-bond fluctuations mediate phonon scattering.
Variations in local chemical environments increase lattice distortion.
Enhanced disorder-related phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes.
Lattice distortion can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering, resulting in low lattice thermal conductivity.
Conventional models ignore detailed local-disorder effects and consequently overestimate lattice thermal conductivity.
Model-selected candidates will have measured lattice thermal conductivities at least 20–30% below values predicted by traditional ab initio approaches.
The proposed model will align more closely with experimental lattice thermal conductivity values than conventional predictions.
Standard DFT and simplified empirical models do not fully account for complex local disorder in high-entropy alloys.
The approach will be most applicable to single-phase, well-mixed high-entropy alloys with moderate disorder and less reliable for multiphase or extremely mismatched systems.
The magnitude of predictive improvement may vary with alloy system, measurement conditions, and the type of disorder.

Failure to observe either a conductivity at least 20% below the conventional prediction or a correlation between disorder descriptors and reduced lattice thermal conductivity will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline says conventional methods provide predictions within a 'smaller accuracy margin' relative to experiment, which ordinarily implies smaller errors, while the hypothesis and predicted outcome claim that the proposed model is more accurate.
